parsed.explanation: The problem is solved using bit manipulation to simulate a half-adder: bitwise XOR computes the sum without carries, while bitwise AND shifted left by one determines the carry, repeating until the carry is zero. This operates in O(b) time—bounded by the fixed bit-width b of the integer—and O(1) space, vastly outperforming naive O(n) unit-increment approaches. While largely an educational exercise in general software engineering due to native CPU addition instructions, the pattern directly underpins hardware ALU design, circuit synthesis, and zero-knowledge proof constraints.
